reason: The sources provide 18 highly detailed, multi-site verified claims about the surprise explosion of the Chelyabinsk meteor on the same day as a predicted asteroid flyby.
story: On February 15, 2013, astronomers were focused on asteroid 367943 Duende, which was predicted to fly safely past Earth. But they were completely blind to another danger. Out of the glare of the Sun, an undetected 10,000-ton asteroid slammed into the atmosphere over Chelyabinsk, Russia, at 19 kilometers per second. It exploded with the energy of 30 Hiroshima bombs, momentarily outshining the Sun. Dashcams captured the spectacular fireball and the rising double-plume. Although the air burst occurred 23 to 30 kilometers high, absorbing most of the energy, it generated a powerful shock wave. Minutes later, the blast shattered glass across six cities, injuring around 1,500 people. Coincidentally, the orbits of the two asteroids showed they were entirely unrelated. Scientists later discovered that the Chelyabinsk rock had experienced a complex history of cosmic collisions, and its orbit matched a much larger asteroid, suggesting it was once part of a larger companion.
angle: An undetected 10,000-ton asteroid blindsided Earth from the direction of the Sun and exploded with the force of 30 Hiroshima bombs on the exact same day astronomers were watching a completely different asteroid fly by.

claims.claim: The Chelyabinsk meteor event occurred on February 15, 2013, over Russia.
The asteroid was approximately 18 to 20 meters in diameter before entering the atmosphere.
The asteroid had an estimated pre-entry mass of about 10,000 to 12,000 tons.
The asteroid entered the atmosphere at a speed of approximately 18.6 to 19.2 kilometers per second.
The asteroid entered the atmosphere at a shallow angle of about 18 degrees.
The asteroid exploded in a meteor air burst at an altitude of about 23 to 30 kilometers above the ground.
The air burst released energy equivalent to approximately 400 to 500 kilotons of TNT.
The explosion's energy was approximately 30 times more powerful than the atomic bomb dropped on Hiroshima.
The meteor produced an intense flash of light that was briefly brighter than the Sun.
The asteroid was undetected prior to impact because it approached Earth from the direction of the Sun, hidden by its glare.
The explosion produced a powerful shock wave that shattered window glass and injured approximately 1,491 to 1,500 people.
The shock wave damaged around 7,200 buildings across the region.
On the same day of the strike, a predicted asteroid named 367943 Duende made a close flyby of Earth.
The orbits of the Chelyabinsk meteor and asteroid Duende were completely different, meaning the two events were unrelated.
The Chelyabinsk meteor was the largest natural space object to enter Earth's atmosphere since the 1908 Tunguska event.
The meteor's orbit was statistically similar to the 2-kilometer-wide asteroid 86039 (1999 NC43), suggesting they once belonged to the same parent body.
Many video recordings of the meteor and explosion were captured by dashboard cameras.
Isotopic analysis of recovered meteor fragments showed the material had undergone multiple past collisions in space over billions of years.

disputed: The mass of the largest recovered fragment from Lake Chebarkul is disputed between Wikipedia articles, with S1 stating 654 kg and S2 stating 540 kg. A script should leave this specific weight out as it only appears on Wikipedia.

The pre-entry mass of the asteroid is estimated differently across sources (S1/S2 say 9,100 tonnes, S3 says 10,000 to 11,000 metric tons, and S7 says 12,000 tons). A script should use a range like 10,000 to 12,000 tons.

The explosive yield has been suggested to be as high as 57 megatons in S1, but S1, S4, S6, and S7 agree on a best estimate of 400 to 500 kilotons. A script should stick to the standard 400 to 500 kiloton range.
